meta.title: Antonio Selvas — Backend & AI
meta.description: Backend developer who brings AI into real products. Node.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL and Flutter.

hero.lead: Software developer specialized in Node.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL. I build APIs, secure authentication and integrations with language models, as well as mobile apps with Flutter.

profile.label: Profile
profile.statement: Solid backends, well-modeled data and AI built into real products.
paragraphs: My work centers on server-side architecture: REST APIs with Node.js and TypeScript, data modeling in PostgreSQL, secure authentication and continuous integration and delivery pipelines with Docker and GitHub Actions.

I complement this with mobile development in Flutter and Kotlin. I'm currently going deeper into bringing language models into products: content generation, automated assessment and conversational experiences.

ravantech.summary: Kotoba is an app for learning English and Mandarin Chinese through voice conversations with an AI agent. I was responsible for building the mobile app.

highlights.title: Architecture.
highlights.text: Set up the project foundation with Clean Architecture, feature-based organization and Riverpod for state management.

highlights.title: Voice conversation.
highlights.text: Built the audio recording, upload and playback flow, with idempotency keys and retries with exponential backoff.

highlights.title: Authentication.
highlights.text: Integrated persistent sessions with Supabase, profiles protected by Row Level Security and route-level access control.

highlights.title: Quality and design.
highlights.text: Set up continuous integration in GitHub Actions as a merge requirement, and a Material 3 design system with semantic tokens.

readflow.description: Turns PDF documents into AI-generated summaries and quizzes, and measures student retention at two points: right after studying and 48 hours later.
highlights: Service-oriented REST API in Node.js and TypeScript
Summaries, quizzes and automated grading with Gemini
JWT authentication with rotating refresh tokens
readflow.secondaryImageAlt: Results of the 48-hour spaced quiz in ReadFlow

warik.description: Runs solutions to technical interview problems step by step and shows the state of every data structure in real time. Built to support educational content about algorithms.
highlights: Python runs directly in the browser, no server required
Visualizes arrays, pointers, dictionaries, stacks, linked lists and trees
Playback, speed controls and keyboard navigation
warik.imageAlt: Warik running Reverse Linked List step by step

laberinto.tagline: An introduction to programming through levels.
laberinto.description: Web game where players solve mazes by writing programs with Spanish-language instructions, applying sequences, loops and conditionals.
highlights: Custom interpreter for a Spanish-language instruction set
Animated execution with a slow-motion mode
